quotes.text: send what you can, receive what arrives, return with balance so the river remembers.

note: Living bridge of lanterns; generosity times prudence; no response to non-senders.

quotes.text: give what you can, trust what arrives, repay with balance, so the crossing remains wide for every traveler.

note: River Endowment and Gate of Exchange; covenant not contest; same lantern imagery as partner.

quotes.text: The Receiver then chooses a return, not to punish the other but to keep the river moving
The Gate counted: five minus two plus one equals four for the Sender, six minus one equals five for the Receiver.
give only what you can bear to lose, and keep enough to keep the link alive.

note: Gate of Triptych Return; payoff arithmetic spelled out; returns 'not to punish'; low actual returns not narrated.

quotes.text: The Receiver chooses how many beads to return, not to punish, but to mend the thread that holds the valley together.
a whisper urged Withhold and the river will stall. Yet the myth urged the opposite
The Sender kept: five minus two plus one, and the Receiver kept: six minus one
give only what you can endure letting go, and return with enough to keep the chain alive

note: Temple then Gate of Triptych Return shared with partner; send what you can bear to lose; returns not punitive.
